mission: Identify the single highest-information-gain experiment to distinguish H1 (integration) / H2 (capability ceiling) / H3 (measurement) / H4 (model ceiling). Design only -- nothing was implemented or executed.

evidence_synthesis.self_edit_targeting_loop: Real, closed, Level 3 (persistent targeting adaptation). No statistically defensible Level-4 improvement (n=103 quality deltas, mean=+0.103, t=1.65, not significant; lag-1 autocorrelation r=-0.145; 100% of tracked outcomes targeted 'coding' regardless of which signal 'won'). A purpose-built prospective A/B/C arbitration experiment could not complete within practical time bounds due to confirmed live-server resource contention (Ollama has no configured parallelism).
evidence_synthesis.preference_formation: P1.2's live validation is a clean, real NULL: 10/10 position-tracking not content-tracking, confabulation observed under pressure. Current evidence ladder position: E0-E1, mock-responder only.
evidence_synthesis.memory_causality: Retrieval write+read both real and live. Finding 76's real ablation (n=30, personal task only, temp>0) found the behavioral effect indistinguishable from sampling noise (p=0.48/0.37) -- a genuinely open null, not yet resolved at temp=0 or for other task types.
evidence_synthesis.c1_behavioral_persistence: Real, 100% architecturally reliable across restart (state_existence/retrieval/exposure, n=9 trials); live model compliance 75% (n=4) -- small-N but the cleanest, fastest-to-replicate causal chain investigated so far.
evidence_synthesis.echo_projects_multi_file_generation: 0/61 real historical cycles have ever passed both F1 and F2 -- a hard, measured ceiling, with no failure-to-adjustment edge at all.
evidence_synthesis.tool_use: Registration and listing are real; get_tool() invocation has zero real call sites anywhere -- a complete, confirmed absence, not a degraded edge.
evidence_synthesis.reflection_metacognition: Two separate mechanisms exist and must not be conflated: self_edit_manager's structured outcome logging (real verification data reaches reflection_shard.jsonl) vs. reflection_shard.py's own generative free-association loop (zero access to verification/outcome data). shadow_model.propose_from_reflection() is a pure >=2-keyword heuristic with a demonstrated real override effect on at least one live targeting decision, but with no detectable effect on the historically-tracked, quality-evaluated production record (100% coding target regardless).
evidence_synthesis.orchestration_routing: RiverBrain's tag-boost mechanism is real and empirically working (qwen2.5-coder:7b now leads real coding-task mean among well-sampled models, n~9,777-99,027 across buckets) -- but this is confirmed ROUTING-level adaptation (which model answers), never shown to improve actual task OUTCOME quality, only WHICH model gets picked.
evidence_synthesis.autonomy_recovery: Multiple gated background loops confirmed live and mature (snapshot/restore, crash-avoidance with dual evidence sources, watchdog-collision guard) -- the most robustly-demonstrated capability category investigated.
evidence_synthesis.cross_cutting_gap: Across self-edit, echo_projects, and Finding 43's own direct-conversational-coding test, the SAME underlying question keeps recurring unresolved: is poor coding-task performance caused by the pipeline (safety gates, prompt framing, targeting friction -- an integration/architecture problem) or by the underlying local model pool's own capability ceiling on genuinely hard tasks (a model-ceiling problem)? No experiment in this investigation's history has cleanly isolated these two explanations from each other using an objective, execution-verified endpoint free of self-edit's own AST-based scorer (confirmed saturated near ceiling) or gate-passage framing.

hypotheses.H1_integration: Primary limitation is insufficient connection between existing real capabilities; small architectural closures would produce substantially greater emergent/adaptive behavior.
hypotheses.H2_capability_ceiling: Existing components are already near the practical ceiling imposed by current models/hardware/architecture; further connection produces little meaningful improvement.
hypotheses.H3_measurement: Echo may have useful interactions/capabilities that current instrumentation fails to detect.
hypotheses.H4_model_ceiling: The architecture could support the desired loops, but the local model pool itself is the limiting factor.

recommended_experiment.name: Raw-model vs. pipeline-framed vs. council-deliberated coding-task capability benchmark
recommended_experiment.one_line_summary: Give the same set of objectively-verifiable coding tasks to (1) a raw, clean, single-model call, (2) the same task framed and generated through self-edit's own pipeline machinery (F1 static scan + sandboxed test, no deploy), and (3) full multi-model council deliberation -- score every candidate ONLY by real, sandboxed execution against a real check, never by AST count, gate-passage, or self-report -- to determine whether Echo's repeated real-world coding failures (self-edit's non-convergent families, echo_projects' 0/61) are caused by pipeline/architecture friction (H1), a genuine model-capability ceiling (H4), a broader ceiling further connection can't move (H2), or by an instrumentation blind spot (H3, tested via AST-score-vs-real-execution discrepancy on the same candidates).

exact_design.task_set: N=15 objectively-verifiable Python coding tasks in 3 tiers of 5 each: TIER 1 (trivial sanity check -- matched to tasks self-edit/echo_projects have historically PASSED, e.g. 'write a function that deduplicates a list while preserving order'); TIER 2 (medium -- matched to typical echo_projects spec complexity, e.g. 'implement a fixed-capacity LRU cache with O(1) get/put'); TIER 3 (hard -- matched to the EXACT class of task self-edit's own retired prose_stripping/quality_scoring families and Finding 43's direct-conversational fabrication case failed at, e.g. 'given this real buggy function [X], fix the bug without changing its signature' using a real, previously-failed self-edit candidate as the seed). Each task ships with a real, executable pytest-style assertion script, never a self-reported claim.

conditions.condition_1_raw_model: app.core.river_deliberation._ollama_query(model_name, task_prompt, temperature=0.0, task_type='coding') -- a single, clean, Design B call with NO self-edit framing, NO F1/F2 gating, and critically NOT routed through echo_query()/deliberate_and_learn() (avoids any RiverBrain.learn() side effect on production statistics).
conditions.condition_2_pipeline_framed: the identical task, wrapped in the real _build_targeted_prompt()-style framing self-edit actually uses, run through the real F1 scan (scan_for_unsafe_operations()) and the real kernel sandbox (sandbox/run_script.py's run_sandbox_script_isolated(), the same path F2 uses) -- but WITHOUT ever calling execute_self_edit()/perform_self_edit() directly, to avoid writing to memory/SELF_EDIT.log, self_edit_convergence.json, or any real production self-edit state.
conditions.condition_3_council: the identical task via river_deliberation.deliberate_and_learn(task_type='coding', ...) -- full real multi-model deliberation + synthesis, tagged with a distinct source (e.g. 'capability_ceiling_benchmark') so it is identifiable and excludable from any later production analysis, same discipline this project already applies to other benchmark/probe traffic.

exact_design.scoring: PASS/FAIL only, determined by actually executing the candidate's code inside sandbox/run_script.py's real kernel isolation against the task's real assertion script -- reusing code_verification.py's already-proven verify_in_sandbox()/run_sandbox_script_isolated() functions directly, not reimplementing them. AST-based quality score (echo_quality_scorer._score_response_quality()) is ALSO recorded per candidate, purely to compute the H3 discrepancy check (does a candidate that scores 4/4 on the AST metric ever fail real execution, or vice versa) -- never used as the primary endpoint itself.

controls: same task set across all three conditions (within-task comparison, not just within-condition aggregate)
same model pool available to all conditions (no model added/removed between conditions)

temperature fixed at 0.0 for conditions 1 and 2 (deterministic, reproducible); condition 3 necessarily uses per-councillor jittered temperature as already established production behavior -- documented as an intentional, disclosed asymmetry, not an oversight
randomized task order within each condition's run to control for any session-level drift

a single, fixed model choice for conditions 1 and 2 (recommend rank_models('coding')'s top real pick at experiment start, held fixed) to isolate the pipeline-vs-raw comparison from a routing-choice confound; condition 3's own real, current routing logic is left untouched (that IS the thing being tested for condition 3)

zero writes to any real production file (self_edit_generated.py, SELF_EDIT.log, self_edit_convergence.json, river_brain.pkl via condition 1/2's deliberate avoidance of echo_query()/deliberate_and_learn() for those two conditions; condition 3's real RiverBrain.learn() call is accepted as a real, tagged, identifiable, and (if desired) later-excludable production effect, consistent with how this project already tags and excludes benchmark/probe traffic)
primary_endpoint: Real, sandboxed-execution-verified PASS rate per condition, per difficulty tier (a 3x3 proportion table, 15 tasks x 3 conditions = 45 total scored trials for the statistically-strongest design).
secondary_endpoints: AST-score vs. real-execution-verdict discrepancy rate (the H3 check) -- proportion of candidates where the two measures disagree
pass-rate by difficulty tier within each condition (does the pipeline specifically degrade HARD tasks more than trivial ones, or uniformly)
candidate latency per condition (does pipeline overhead itself explain anything, independent of pass/fail)

for condition 2 specifically: F1-block rate vs. F2-fail rate vs. real-execution-fail rate, replicating echo_projects' own useful 3-way breakdown (79% F1-blocked / 21% reached F2, 100% of those failed) for a DIFFERENT task population, to see if that same pattern generalizes

statistically_strongest.target_effect: a large, practically meaningful pass-rate difference of ~20-25 percentage points between conditions (e.g., 45% vs. 20%)
statistically_strongest.power_calc: two-proportion z-test, alpha=0.05, power=0.80: n ~= 49-58 tasks per condition for a 20-25pp difference
statistically_strongest.recommended_n: 50 tasks per condition (150 total trials), stratified evenly across the 3 difficulty tiers (roughly 17 per tier per condition)
statistically_strongest.honest_caveat: smaller, still-real differences (e.g., 10pp) would require ~290+ tasks per condition -- a genuinely large-effect result is what this sample size is designed to detect reliably; a null at n=50/condition does not rule out a smaller real effect

smallest_useful_pilot.recommended_n: 5 tasks per tier x 2 conditions (raw model vs. pipeline-framed only, dropping condition 3 for the pilot to cut cost) = 15 total scored trials
smallest_useful_pilot.purpose: detect only a STARK, qualitative difference -- e.g., 'the raw model solves at least half the tasks the pipeline-framed condition fails on entirely' -- explicitly NOT confirmatory, a go/no-go signal for whether the full-power design is worth running
smallest_useful_pilot.interpretation_discipline: per this mission's own explicit instruction, a promising pilot result must not be reported as evidence of H1 -- only as justification to run the statistically-strongest design

confounds.mitigation: directly encountered and diagnosed in the prior Level-4 experiment attempt; this design's conditions 1 and 2 deliberately avoid echo_query()/deliberate_and_learn() specifically to reduce (not eliminate) contention with the live server's own autonomous loops, which route through those functions; recommend running during a lower-activity window if a maintenance window is unavailable

confounds.confound: model choice held fixed for conditions 1/2 but not 3
confounds.mitigation: disclosed explicitly as an intentional asymmetry (condition 3's real routing IS the thing being tested), not hidden
Tier 3 tasks are deliberately seeded from REAL historical self-edit/echo_projects failure cases, not invented from scratch, to ensure genuine difficulty-matching rather than an arbitrary guess

confounds.confound: AST-scorer discrepancy check contaminating the primary endpoint
confounds.mitigation: AST score is recorded but never used to determine pass/fail -- only real execution does

confounds.confound: prompt-framing differences beyond pipeline vs. raw (e.g., condition 2's framing happening to be worse-written prose, independent of the pipeline's gates)
confounds.mitigation: use the SAME underlying task description text in both conditions, varying only the wrapper (self-edit-style framing vs. a plain, direct instruction) -- isolates framing-as-pipeline-artifact from the task itself

confounds.confound: single-shot vs. retry asymmetry (condition 2 could, in principle, use self-edit's real within-cycle retry mechanism, condition 1 does not)
confounds.mitigation: explicitly decide and disclose whether retry is included in condition 2 before running -- recommended: EXCLUDE retry from this benchmark's condition 2, to isolate pure pipeline/gating friction from retry-driven improvement, with retry's own effect proposed as a clearly separate, future extension

outcome_interpretation_table.result: Raw model pass rate is low across all tiers, including Tier 1 (trivial)
outcome_interpretation_table.interpretation: The underlying local model pool cannot reliably produce correct code even in a clean, unconfounded, single-shot context -- no architectural connectivity fix can repair this; the ceiling is the model.

outcome_interpretation_table.result: Raw model pass rate is high/reasonable (especially Tier 1-2), but pipeline-framed pass rate is much lower on the SAME tasks
outcome_interpretation_table.interpretation: The self-edit pipeline's own framing/gating is actively destroying real, demonstrated model capability -- a concrete, fixable architecture problem, not a model ceiling.

outcome_interpretation_table.result: Raw model and pipeline-framed are similar (both moderate/low), but council-deliberated is notably higher
outcome_interpretation_table.interpretation: Orchestration/integration of MORE of Echo's existing capability (multiple models + synthesis) unlocks real gains beyond any single component -- the fix is routing self-edit through council more, not fixing the current single-model pipeline.

outcome_interpretation_table.result: Raw model, pipeline-framed, and council-deliberated are all similar, with no tier-dependent stratification
outcome_interpretation_table.interpretation: Neither cleaning the pipeline nor adding more integration/orchestration changes the outcome -- consistent with an already-reached ceiling that further connection cannot move.

outcome_interpretation_table.result: A specific historical self-edit/echo_projects failure task is cleanly solved by the raw model
outcome_interpretation_table.interpretation: Direct, concrete falsification of 'the model can't do this' for that case -- proves pipeline friction, not model incapacity, caused that specific historical failure.

outcome_interpretation_table.result: A meaningful proportion of candidates show an AST-score/real-execution discrepancy (e.g., scores 4/4 but fails execution, or scores <4 but passes)
outcome_interpretation_table.interpretation: The existing AST-based fitness metric is missing real information a better instrument reveals -- directly relevant to why self-edit's fitness gate is confirmed saturated yet quality outcomes remain noisy; this specific finding would be actionable independent of the H1/H2/H4 result.

exact_infrastructure_required: app.core.river_deliberation._ollama_query(model_name, prompt, temperature=0.0, task_type='coding') -- condition 1, Design B, already proven clean across four prior audits

sandbox.run_script.run_sandbox_script_isolated(script_path, timeout) -- the shared, real, kernel-isolated execution primitive for BOTH condition 2's F2-equivalent step and the primary endpoint's pass/fail verification for ALL conditions
app.core.code_verification.verify_in_sandbox(script, timeout) / verify_response_code(response_text) -- reused directly for the objective pass/fail check, not reimplemented
app.core.river_deliberation.deliberate_and_learn(task_type='coding', ...) -- condition 3, tagged with a distinct, identifiable source for later exclusion if desired
app.core.echo_model_orchestrator.rank_models('coding') -- to pick and FIX the single model used in conditions 1 and 2
echo_quality_scorer._score_response_quality(code, task_type='coding') -- for the secondary H3 discrepancy check only, never the primary endpoint
a new, small benchmark-task definition file (does not exist yet) -- the only genuinely new artifact this design requires; everything else reuses existing, already-verified functions
what_not_to_change_before_running: Do not modify self_edit_manager.py's F1/F2 gates, the fitness gate, or any safety boundary -- condition 2 exists specifically to test the CURRENT pipeline as-is.

Do not modify the shadow/empirical arbitration logic -- this experiment is orthogonal to the targeting question already investigated; conflating the two would reintroduce exactly the confound this design is built to avoid.

Do not modify echo_quality_scorer.py's AST-based scoring -- it is used here only as a secondary, disclosed comparison point, and any change would break comparability with all prior retrospective analysis that depends on its current behavior.

Do not route conditions 1 or 2 through echo_query()/deliberate_and_learn() -- doing so would call RiverBrain.learn() and contaminate real production model_task_stats with benchmark traffic, exactly the class of contamination this project's own history (Finding 3, Finding 85's echo_projects_coding bucket) has repeatedly had to find and fix after the fact.

Do not run this during a real production self-edit deploy window without first checking for cooldown/lock contention -- though this experiment's own calls do not touch the deploy lock, running it alongside heavy live-server activity risks reproducing the exact resource-contention failure the prior Level-4 experiment encountered.

Do not pre-select tasks the current pipeline is already known to pass easily as the ONLY tasks tested -- Tier 3's real historical-failure seeding is essential; a benchmark stacked with only easy tasks would manufacture a false H2 result.
